Compute Screener

Methodology

GPU prices are currently based on Compute Rental Prices and will transition to Compute Futures Prices as the market matures (see below).

Compute Screener, built and run by @RenshuBTC, publishes a daily GPU Price Index for each GPU family and a daily Token Price Index for each AI company. Every value is calculated automatically by the rules below and can be recomputed from the published data.

GPU Price IndexToken Price Index
MeasuresThe on-demand rental price of a GPU family at neo-cloud providers and GPU marketplacesThe posted API price of a company's models, weighted by their usage
UnitUSD / GPU-hourUSD / 1M tokens, at a mix of 87% cache reads, 12% input and 1% output
DayCalendar day in US Central TimeUTC day
UpdatedEvery minute; provisional during the day, final when it endsOnce a day, shortly after the day ends
Version4.1, from 2026-10-242.0, from 2026-10-28

Compute Rental Prices and Compute Futures Prices

The GPU prices on this site, on the Compute tab and at the top of each GPU's page, are currently based on Compute Rental Prices: the GPU Price Index below, built from the on-demand prices that cloud providers and GPU marketplaces post. They will transition to Compute Futures Prices, the prices of exchange-traded contracts on a GPU's rental price, as that market matures.

As of October 2026, compute futures trade on two GPUs, H100 and B200, as perpetual contracts; most of their 24-hour volume is on one exchange, and the futures announced by CME Group and ICE are not trading yet. Until the market is deeper, each GPU's page shows every exchange's own last price and 24-hour volume under Compute Futures Prices, and those prices do not enter any index. The change will be announced on this page at least 14 days before it applies, like any material change (see Changes under Governance).

GPU Price Index

Indices for H100, H200, A100, B200, B300, MI300X and RTX PRO 6000, and from 2026-10-28 for L40S and RTX A6000, whose indices are calculated and published in the data files below but not yet shown on the site. A GPU is added once a whole day of collection prices it at the 5 providers a value needs (see Publication); the RTX 6000 Ada, L40, RTX 5090, RTX 4090 and RTX A4000 are collected until then. The posted prices of every GPU whose index is not shown are on Every GPU. Hyperscalers such as AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and Oracle are not included; a GPU's page lists the posted prices of providers outside the index (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle, Akamai, Koyeb and Packet) beside its index, under Other Posted Prices, as posted and not standardized. Every price is converted to its GPU's benchmark contract:

IndexBenchmark contract
  1. Collect. The index reads posted on-demand prices from each provider's API or pricing page, each on its own interval: the Vast.ai, Lium, RunPod, Akash and Shadeform marketplaces every minute, the Verda, Scaleway and Vultr catalogues every 5 minutes, and the other providers' price lists every 30 minutes, since they rarely change and reading them more often risks being blocked. CoreWeave's page refuses requests from the network the live collection runs on, so the scheduled update reads it, several times a day, and each of those readings counts at the time it was read. The index is recalculated every minute. An offer's price for the day is the average of the readings at which it had capacity, so a source read more often does not weigh more. If this live collection stops, a scheduled update reads every source several times a day until it resumes. The sources are rate cards, every ask on the Vast.ai and Lium marketplaces, and Akash's average ask. Other smaller clouds are read from Shadeform's public catalog, which also shows their capacity. Each API, page or catalog counts as one source, and no cloud is read through two for the same GPU. Euro prices are converted at the European Central Bank's rate of the day.
  2. Filter. Where a source shows capacity, a provider counts for a GPU only if one of its offers had capacity at some collection that day; its posted prices then all count, so an offer selling out does not read as a price change. Asks more than 2× from their marketplace's median and prices more than 2.5× from the GPU's historical reference are left out. A marketplace counts for a GPU only with at least 3 usable asks from at least 2 hosts.
  3. Check. A provider's price that moves more than 35% from its 14-day median is held out until the new level has lasted 3 days, unless the market moved with it: net of the median move of at least 3 other sources, it moved less than 35%. A move shared by most of the clouds read through one catalog, and not by other sources, is treated as that catalog's error and stays held.
  4. Standardize. Each price is divided by factors for how it differs from the benchmark: form factor and memory, GPUs per rental, region and CPU. Factors are estimated weekly over 28 days from providers that price both configurations on the same day, and need comparisons from at least 2 providers, or 5 matched groups for region and CPU. Without them, a price with another form factor or memory is left out and other differences are not adjusted. The factors for GPUs per rental, region and CPU are estimated on the first seven GPUs, H100 to RTX PRO 6000, and applied to every GPU, so adding a GPU does not change them. Each GPU added later is one card with one form factor and memory, its benchmark; a listing with other memory, such as an RTX 4090 modified to 48 GB, is left out.
  5. Average. Each provider's prices are averaged, so a provider counts once however many listings it has. A provider with no price on a day is carried for up to 7 days, moved by the other providers' average change.
  6. Chain. The index moves by the geometric mean of the price changes of providers priced both on the day and on the last published day:index today = index last × geometric mean of (provider average today ÷ provider average last)Itoday=Ilast×(∏i=1npˉi,todaypˉi,last)1/nI_{\text{today}} = I_{\text{last}} \times \left( \prod_{i=1}^{n} \frac{\bar{p}_{i,\text{today}}}{\bar{p}_{i,\text{last}}} \right)^{1/n}Itoday​=Ilast​×(i=1∏n​pˉ​i,last​pˉ​i,today​​)1/nwhere pˉi\bar{p}_ipˉ​i​ is the average price of provider iii and nnn is the number of providers priced on both days. Both averages use today's standardization factors, so a recalibration does not move the index, and providers joining or leaving do not move it either.
FactorCurrent values

Publication. A value needs at least 5 matched providers, 3 of them priced that day, so no provider weighs more than 20%. A new provider counts after 14 days of collection; the 15 added by version 4.1 count at once, from their second day of prices. For a GPU added later, the providers first priced in its first 14 days count at once, and its index starts at the cross-section average on the first day at least 5 providers are priced. If no value was published in the previous 7 days, the index restarts at the cross-section average: the mean of all provider averages with the most extreme ones clipped.

Also published each day: the cross-section average and the quartiles of the provider averages, and monthly averages of the index in /data/index.json.

History. Live values start on 2026-10-23. Before that, H100 and A100 have daily history from 2025-11-07, rebuilt with this methodology from the posted prices in SkyPilot's open price catalog, 5 to 8 providers a day; only these two have 90 days of it without a break. Earlier, and for H200, B200, B300 and RTX PRO 6000, history is weekly: GetDeploying's on-demand median across providers, in weeks with at least 5. Each earlier series is scaled to meet the later one, so a change of source does not move the index. L40S and RTX A6000 start on 2026-10-28, with GetDeploying's weekly history joined on that day. A GPU added later is joined on its first day, in the dataset week that contains it; its history is left out when the dataset's value that week is more than 25% from the median of the three weeks before, as happens when a thin week's providers change.

Token Price Index

One index for each AI company in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index chart (version 4.3.2, October 2026) whose models are used through OpenRouter: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI, Meta, Moonshot AI, Alibaba, DeepSeek, Z.ai, Xiaomi, StepFun, MiniMax, Mistral, Reflection AI, NVIDIA and Thinking Machines. A day's value is what the company's paid tokens cost that day at the mix of tokens that agents send: the average price of its models, weighted by their tokens:index = Σ (tokens × price) ÷ Σ tokensI=∑jqj Pj∑jqjI = \frac{\sum_{j} q_j \, P_j}{\sum_{j} q_j}I=∑j​qj​∑j​qj​Pj​​where qjq_jqj​ is the number of tokens of model jjj that day and PjP_jPj​ is its price at the mix.

  • Tokens are each model's daily prompt and completion tokens in OpenRouter's daily rankings of the top 50 models.
  • The mix. A model's price is its posted price for the mix of tokens OpenRouter measured in agentic use in September 2026, "roughly 87% cached, 12% novel prompt, 1% output" (OpenRouter, Inferred 03, 8 October 2026):price = 0.87 × cache read price + 0.12 × input price + 0.01 × output priceP=0.87 Pcache+0.12 Pin+0.01 PoutP = 0.87\,P_{\text{cache}} + 0.12\,P_{\text{in}} + 0.01\,P_{\text{out}}P=0.87Pcache​+0.12Pin​+0.01Pout​A cache read is a prompt token served from the provider's prompt cache. A model with no cache price has no cache discount, so its cache read price is its input price. Cache writes are not counted. The mix is the same every day, so the index moves only with prices and with which models are used, not with how much buyers cache.
  • Prices are the company's own posted standard prices: no batch, priority or long-context pricing. Where a price depends on the hour, the rate in force for most of the week counts: DeepSeek bills twice its base rate in its weekday peak hours, 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC. They are read from the company's own endpoint on OpenRouter shortly after each UTC day ends; if that endpoint is briefly missing, the price read up to 3 days before is kept.
  • Companies that sell no API of their own. NVIDIA, Thinking Machines and Reflection AI release their models' weights and do not sell the models themselves. Their models are priced at the median posted price of the providers that serve them on OpenRouter, each at its standard tier, ranked at the mix.
  • Models that count are paid text models. Free variants, batch tiers, embedding, image and safety models, and OpenAI's and Google's open-weight releases, gpt-oss and Gemma, are left out. A model with published weights from a company that sells its own API counts only while the company itself serves it, since other hosts sell it too.
  • Days without a countable model. A company with no countable model in the day's top 50 is priced with its last model weights: the shares of its models on the last day it had some, repriced at that day's prices. Such a day is marked in the data (c: the day the weights are from).
  • Coverage. A value is published only when models with a known price carry at least 80% of the tokens that count, or of the carried weights.
  • List price. The blend of version 1, list prices at 3 input tokens to 1 output token, is kept beside each value for comparison:list price = (3 × input price + output price) ÷ 4Plist=3 Pin+Pout4P_{\text{list}} = \frac{3\,P_{\text{in}} + P_{\text{out}}}{4}Plist​=43Pin​+Pout​​
  • Estimated spend through OpenRouter is each day's Σ tokens × price ÷ 106, in USD, with the last 30 days' total and a year at that rate (× 365 ÷ 30). Only the company's paid models in the top 50 count, so these figures are floors, not its revenue.

History. Daily from 2025-01-01, from OpenRouter's rankings dataset as stored in /data/legacy/openrouter_rankings.json.gz, at each day's prices: first the company's own dated announcements and records, such as DeepSeek's change log and price notices, Xiaomi's update log and announcements, Moonshot AI's model list, StepFun's and Alibaba's notices and Google's and xAI's pricing pages and release notes; then the dated history at llm-prices.com by Simon Willison; then the prices read on version 1's live days, 2026-10-22 to 2026-10-27; and otherwise today's price, which assumes it never changed. A cache price not on record is today's cache discount on the company's own endpoint applied to the day's input price; with neither, the model's price is unknown. Where a company's records date when it served each version, those dates decide which versions count, and a version served free does not count. Otherwise an open-weight model the company serves today counts from its release, and a day is left empty when versions of unknown service or price carry more than 20% of the tokens. DeepSeek's history starts on 2026-08-17, the first full day of its current pricing.

Version 1, until 2026-10-27, priced ten companies at the 3:1 list-price blend. On 2026-10-28, at the owner's decision, version 2.0 replaced it and all token history was recomputed with it. Version 1's series, history and latest values stay downloadable in /data/legacy/token_v1/, and its final days' manifests and traces are kept unchanged.

Listing

A GPU or company is listed once it has a price and a month of history (its first value at least 30 days before its latest). A change is measured against the value that many days earlier. Where the history has no value that day (the weekly history before a GPU's daily index began, or a day with no value), it is measured against the value interpolated in a straight line between the nearest values before and after that day, if they are at most 14 days apart; the change cell says so when hovered. DeepSeek is always listed. MI300X is collected but not yet published, because fewer than 5 providers price it.

Price trend

The Compute tab lists the GPUs, and the Tokens tab the AI companies, by the strength of their price trend over the last 13 weeks, strongest first, whether the price is rising or falling.

  1. Prices. The GPU's or company's index on 13 dates a week apart, ending with the latest value (during the day, the provisional value).
  2. Line. A straight line fitted by least squares to the logarithms of those prices, week by week:ln(price) = intercept + slope × weekln⁡pk=a+b k+ek,k=0,1,…,12\ln p_k = a + b\,k + e_k, \qquad k = 0, 1, \ldots, 12lnpk​=a+bk+ek​,k=0,1,…,12where pkp_kpk​ is the price in week kkk, bbb is the fitted slope and eke_kek​ are the residuals. The slope is the trend's speed, shown per month:speed per month = e^(slope × 52 ÷ 12) − 1speed=e52 b/12−1\text{speed} = e^{52\,b/12} - 1speed=e52b/12−1
  3. Score. The slope divided by its standard error, the t-statistic of the slope: large when the price moved steadily one way, small when it moved little or back and forth.score = slope ÷ standard error of the slopet=bSE⁡(b)t = \frac{b}{\operatorname{SE}(b)}t=SE(b)b​SE⁡(b)=∑kek2 / (13−2)∑k(k−6)2\operatorname{SE}(b) = \sqrt{\frac{\sum_k e_k^2 \,/\, (13 - 2)}{\sum_k (k - 6)^2}}SE(b)=∑k​(k−6)2∑k​ek2​/(13−2)​​

Strength. Strong: a score of 4 or more, up or down. Moderate: 2 to 4. Weak: under 2, a move noise alone often makes. The arrow shows the direction. A GPU or company with less than 12 weeks of history has no score and is listed last.

Why this measure. On the index history, from 24 January to 26 September 2026, the GPU with the strongest score kept its direction over the next 4 weeks in 29 of 36 weeks, and following it gained 2.3% on average. The GPU with the largest 1-week change kept its direction in 11 of 26 weeks, and following it lost 1.1%: large weekly moves in GPU rental prices tend to partly reverse, while steady 13-week trends more often continued. One year of six GPUs is a small sample, so this is evidence, not a forecast. The Tokens tab uses the same measure on each company's token index; it was tested on the GPU indices only.

Break-even throughput and gross margin

Each model's page shows its break-even throughput on each GPU: the tokens per second one GPU must generate, sold at the model's list price (3 input tokens to 1 output token, as in the Token Price Index), for its revenue to cover the GPU's rental price today. Each GPU's page shows the same for every model in the Token Price Index. The gross margin calculator on each model's page compares the revenue one GPU earns in an hour with its rental price.

  1. Revenue per GPU-hour. The tokens one GPU generates in an hour, sold at the model's list price:revenue per GPU-hour = throughput × 3,600 × list price ÷ 1,000,000R=3600×T×P106R = \frac{3600 \times T \times P}{10^{6}}R=1063600×T×P​ The calculator also works the other way, from a revenue to the throughput that earns it:throughput = revenue per GPU-hour × 1,000,000 ÷ (3,600 × list price)T=106×R3600×PT = \frac{10^{6} \times R}{3600 \times P}T=3600×P106×R​
  2. Gross profit per GPU-hour. Revenue less the GPU's rental price:gross profit per GPU-hour = revenue per GPU-hour − GPU rental priceG=R−CG = R - CG=R−C
  3. Gross margin. Gross profit as a share of revenue:gross margin = gross profit ÷ revenue per GPU-hourM=GR=1−CRM = \frac{G}{R} = 1 - \frac{C}{R}M=RG​=1−RC​
  4. Break-even throughput. The throughput at which revenue equals the rental price, so gross profit is zero:break-even throughput = GPU rental price × 1,000,000 ÷ (3,600 × list price)TBE=106×C3600×PT_{\text{BE}} = \frac{10^{6} \times C}{3600 \times P}TBE​=3600×P106×C​

where TTT is throughput in tokens per second per GPU, PPP is the model's list price in USD per 1M tokens, CCC is the GPU's rental price in USD per GPU-hour (its GPU Price Index today), RRR and GGG are revenue and gross profit in USD per GPU-hour, and MMM is gross margin.

Example. At a rental price of $3.00 per GPU-hour and a list price of $1.00 per 1M tokens, break-even throughput is 833 tokens per second per GPU. At 5,000 tokens per second, revenue is $18.00 per GPU-hour, gross profit $15.00 and gross margin 83%.

Throughput is entered by the visitor, or worked out from the revenue entered; Compute Screener does not measure it. It counts input and output tokens together, in the 3 to 1 mix of the list price, and depends on the model, the GPU, the serving software, batch size and context length. For a deployment on many GPUs, it is the deployment's tokens per second divided by its number of GPUs. Worked out from a revenue, it is the throughput that earns that revenue at the 3 to 1 mix of posted prices; the mix, cache hits and discounts behind a company's reported revenue can differ, and so can its actual throughput.

Limits. List prices are the posted base input and output rates, without cache or batch discounts (the Token Price Index itself prices the cache-heavy mix above). Gross margin here counts only the GPU's rental price as cost, not networking, storage, staff or idle time, and assumes the GPU generates that throughput for the whole hour.

Reported figures. A company's own figure is shown as the company reported it, without verification. DeepSeek reported overall revenue of US$38 per GPU-hour for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at its off-peak ("valley") prices, from a cluster serving 155 trillion tokens a day, in the deployment Q&A it published with its DeepInfer inference framework in October 2026. It does not say which GPUs earn it.

Data

Every value can be recomputed from these public files, kept for five years:

FileHolds
/data/readings/<day>.json.gzFrom 2026-10-28, every GPU price reading at every collection, with its time: each offer's price per GPU-hour as posted and whether it had capacity (summed, they give the day's records)
/data/records/<day>.json.gzEach offer read that day, with its source page, configuration and latest price, and how many readings it had with and without capacity and their sums
/data/trace/<day>.json.gzEach price used, with its factor, or left out, with the reason; provider averages, chain ratio and matched providers
/data/model.json, /data/stats.jsonStandardization factors and the comparisons behind them; validation references and imputation inputs
/data/index.json, /data/series.jsonLatest GPU values with their providers; full history
/data/token_trace/<day>.json.gz, /data/tokens.json, /data/token_series.jsonEach company's models, tokens, input, output and cache read prices and shares by day, with the day's full OpenRouter rankings and the posted prices of the chart's models; latest values; full history
/data/legacy/History inputs and joins: skypilot_daily.json, getdeploying_weekly.json, history_link.json, token_history.json, llm_prices.json, openrouter_rankings.json.gz (OpenRouter's daily rankings dataset from 2025-01-01, CC BY 4.0); version 1 of the token index: token_v1/; every correction with its reason: restatements.json
/data/manifests/gpu/<day>.json, /data/manifests/tokens/<day>.json, /data/manifests/index.jsonEach final day's manifest: every file the day was computed from with its SHA-256, the final values, and the SHA-256 of the calculation code
/data/state/<day>.json.gzEach final GPU day's stored state, which the following days' calculation reads
/data/gpu_market.jsonGPUs whose index is not shown (RTX 5090, RTX 4090, L40S and others; a GPU leaves it when its index is shown): each model's offers per day in RunPod, Vast.ai, Akash, Shadeform's catalog, Lium, Vultr and the price lists of AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle, Akamai, Koyeb and Packet, the lowest, median and highest price per GPU-hour as posted, without standardizing configurations. Not an index; shown on Every GPU.
/data/outside.jsonEach indexed GPU's posted prices at providers outside the index (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle, Akamai, Koyeb and Packet, from their own price lists): each one's lowest on-demand price per GPU-hour as posted, its number of offers and the memory per GPU of the lowest, read every two hours. Not in the index; shown on the GPU's page under Other Posted Prices.
/data/token_volume.json, /data/token_spend.jsonTokens each company's models processed per UTC day on OpenRouter, the volumes that weight the token index; and their estimated spend at the index's mix and at list prices, with the last 30 days' total and a year at that rate.
/data/errata.jsonAny error found in a final value, with the correct figure and the reason (the final value itself is not changed)

The calculation code and a verifier that recomputes any final value from these files, checking every file against the day's manifest, are published in github.com/renshuBTC/compute-screener, where a scheduled job runs it on every final day, every day. To check one value: python verify.py --date 2026-10-25 --gpu H100. From 2026-10-28 the check starts from the price readings: they are summed again into each offer's records before the index is recomputed (python verify.py --date 2026-10-28 --readings rebuilds any day's records, final or not). The code that reads the providers' prices is not published.

Governance

Inputs. The GPU index uses posted prices and marketplace asks, which anyone can rent at, not executed transactions, which are not public. Indices of executed rentals can differ, usually lower, because large buyers negotiate their rates. Providers weigh equally because their rental volumes are not public.

Control. Values are calculated automatically, never set by judgment, and each run passes automated checks before it is published. A GPU index move above 5% in a day is reviewed, and a review can only confirm a value or correct an error.

Independence. No provider or company pays to be included, and no link affects the index or the order of providers. Compute Screener and the person who runs it hold no futures, swaps, prediction-market contracts or other instruments that settle on GPU rental or AI token prices, and no direct holdings in the providers or companies on this site.

Final values. A value is provisional until its day ends (midnight US Central for GPUs, midnight UTC for AI tokens), then final. From 2026-10-27, a final value is never changed. Each final day has a manifest, and anyone can recompute it (see Data). If an error is found in a final value, the value stays as published: the correct figure and the reason are recorded in /data/errata.json, and the error is fixed from the next day. A new method version applies from its start date and does not recompute earlier days, with one exception: Token Price Index 2.0 recomputed all token history at the owner's decision, and version 1's values stay downloadable (see Token Price Index). Restatements of history, made when versions 4.0 and 4.1 of the GPU index and 2.0 of the token index were introduced, are recorded with their dates, ranges and reasons in /data/legacy/restatements.json.

Changes. A material change to the formula, inputs, filters, benchmark contracts or which providers and models count is announced here at least 14 days before it applies, with its version and date. The one exception: on 2026-10-28 the owner waived the notice for Token Price Index 2.0, which applied the same day. Comments can be sent to the contact on the Privacy page, and a summary is published with the change. A fix to an error applies from the next day and is announced when made. A new index changes nothing in the existing ones, so it starts without notice. Latest: on 2026-10-28, Token Price Index 2.0 replaced the list-price blend with each model's posted prices at OpenRouter's measured agentic mix (87% cache reads, 12% input, 1% output), added StepFun, MiniMax, Mistral, Reflection AI, NVIDIA and Thinking Machines, priced a company with no countable model on a day at its last model weights, added each company's estimated spend, and recomputed all token history from 2025-01-01; version 1 stays in /data/legacy/token_v1/. The same day, version 4.2 added indices for the L40S and the RTX A6000, at the owner's request to price as many GPUs as the method allows; they are calculated and published in the data files, and the owner decides when the site shows them. The seven existing indices are unchanged, with the same inputs, factors and calculation: the new code recomputes every earlier final day exactly. Before that, on 2026-10-27, four errors in the calculation code were fixed, each from that day. First, a token price was read as it stood at the moment of reading, so DeepSeek's value for 2026-10-26 was taken in its peak hours, at twice its base rate; it is recorded in the errata. Second, the check that leaves out an ask more than 2× from its provider's median was applied to every provider, not only to marketplace asks as stated above. It changed one final value, A100 on 2026-10-26, which is recorded in the errata. For the next days, a cloud is compared with the days before the fix without the offers the old check left out, so the fix does not move the index. Third, a recalibration could move the index, because the last published day's stored offers left out the offers that had no factor until then, and an imputed provider's change mixed old and new factors. Every earlier day is now compared in the day's own factors. No recalibration has happened since 4.1, so no published value was affected. Fourth, when two or more providers were imputed from the same day, a provider imputed first was counted, in the next one's change, as if it had been priced, contrary to the imputation rule (GPU Price Index: only providers priced on both days count). It changed no published value. The same day, final values became final without restatement (above), and each final day got a manifest and a public verifier. Before that: on 2026-10-25 at 18:05 UTC, at the owner's request, prices began to be read every 1 to 30 minutes, depending on the source, instead of every 2 to 3 hours, and the GPU index is recalculated every minute. The method is unchanged, so this applied at once. On 2026-10-24, version 4.1 added 15 providers, the capacity rule, the marketplace minimum and the market check on large moves, and compares each provider's prices on one set of factors. The owner applied it at once, without the usual 14 days' notice, and its new providers count at once instead of after 14 days of collection. H100 and A100 history was rebuilt with it. Earlier that day, version 4.0 introduced the chained GPU index and daily H100 and A100 history, and the token histories of DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Xiaomi and Alibaba were corrected from those companies' own records.

Third parties. The calculation runs on Cloudflare every minute, with GitHub Actions as a backup several times a day (scheduled every 2 hours; GitHub starts scheduled runs late or skips them), and the site on Cloudflare Pages. If the ECB rate cannot be read, the last rate up to 7 days old is used, and after that euro prices are left out. A source that fails contributes nothing that run; the latest status of each is below and on the status page.

Licence. The values and data on this site are licensed CC BY 4.0: anyone may reuse them, including commercially, with credit to "Compute Screener (computescreener.com)" (see the terms). Third-party data keeps its own terms: CC BY 4.0 for GetDeploying and OpenRouter, Apache-2.0 for SkyPilot's catalog.

Continuity. An index that cannot be calculated reliably is not published until it can be; its history stays available. If an index stays unpublished for 30 days in a row, or is to be stopped for any other reason, a notice is published here at least 90 days before it ends, naming a successor if there is one, and its history stays available under CC BY 4.0.

Questions and complaints go to the contact on the Privacy page. A complaint about a value or the method is acknowledged within 2 business days and answered within 10. A complaint that leads to a fix or a change is summarized on this page.

IOSCO principles: self-assessment

How the indices meet the 19 IOSCO Principles for Financial Benchmarks (July 2013), assessed by Compute Screener itself, not by a third party. Where a principle is not fully met, the gap is stated.

PrincipleHow it is metGap
1. Overall responsibilityCompute Screener administers both indices: their design, data collection, calculation, publication and governance, all described on this page.One person runs the site; there is no separate legal entity or board.
2. Oversight of third partiesPrices come from providers' public price lists and APIs; the calculation runs on Cloudflare with GitHub Actions as a backup, and the site on Cloudflare Pages (Governance). Each source's status is on the status page.No contracts with the sources: they can change or withdraw their prices at any time.
3. Conflicts of interestNo provider or company pays to be included, and no link affects an index or the order of providers. The administrator holds no instrument that settles on these prices and no direct holding in the providers or companies (Independence).—
4. Control frameworkEvery calculation passes automated checks before it is published; a failed check blocks publication. A GPU index move above 5% in a day is reviewed. Each final day has a checksum manifest.—
5. Internal oversightPublication rules, checks and changes are documented here and in the public verifier.No separate oversight committee. In its place, the data, the calculation code and a verifier are public, and the verifier recomputes every final value daily.
6. Benchmark designEach GPU index prices one benchmark contract (on-demand, 8-GPU node, US), standardizing other configurations to it; each token index is a company's posted prices weighted by its models' usage (GPU Price Index, Token Price Index).Posted prices, not executed rentals (Inputs).
7. Data sufficiencyA GPU value needs at least 5 matched providers, 3 priced that day, so none weighs more than 20%; a token value needs 80% usage coverage. An index without enough data is not published (MI300X today).—
8. Hierarchy of data inputsPrices of offers with capacity come first; a posted price without capacity counts only when its provider had capacity elsewhere; a provider with no price that day is carried from its last reading for up to 7 days, and the share carried is published.Executed transaction prices are not public, so they are not used.
9. Transparency of determinationsEvery price collected (records), what was used or left out and why (trace), and each day's state are published, with a manifest per final day.—
10. Periodic reviewStandardization factors are recalibrated with dated history (model.json); the methodology is reviewed at least once a year, next by October 2027.—
11. Content of the methodologyThis page: definitions, inputs, filters, calculation, imputation, holds, publication rules, finality and governance.—
12. Changes to the methodologyAnnounced here at least 14 days before they apply, with version and date, without exception; comments invited and summarized (Changes).—
13. TransitionAt least 90 days' notice before an index ends, naming a successor if there is one; history stays available (Continuity).—
14. Submitter code of conductNot applicable: no one submits data; prices are collected from public sources.—
15. Controls over data collectionEach source is read on a schedule; parsing, coverage and outlier checks run on every collection, and a failed source contributes nothing that run.—
16. ComplaintsAcknowledged within 2 business days and answered within 10; complaints leading to a fix or change are summarized here.—
17. AuditsAnyone can recompute any final value with the published verifier, and a scheduled public job does so every day.No external audit yet.
18. Audit trailRecords, traces and stored state are kept five years; manifests are written once and never changed; every change to the code and data is in version control.—
19. Cooperation with regulatorsRecords, data and code will be made available to a competent authority on request.—
